## Consolidated implications for running llama.cpp

1. **Mode:** use `fast` (QEMU functional). `cycle`/`hybrid` (kHz) cannot run a full inference in reasonable time.
2. **Memory:** hard **2 GiB total** guest RAM (`fast` gets QEMU's 128 MiB default unless you pass `--mem-size`, which forwards to `-m`; >2 G fails in QEMU). No file `mmap` → build llama.cpp `--no-mmap`; the model is `read()` into heap, so a 700 MB model + KV cache + compute buffers must fit under 2 GiB.
3. **Heap/stack:** relink with a high `_stack` (`-Wl,--defsym,_stack=…`) matched to `--mem-size`; `_sbrk` has no guard (silent collision).
4. **Timing:** patch `ggml_time_us`/`_ms` off `clock_gettime`/`CLOCK_MONOTONIC` onto `gettimeofday` (the only implemented clock); no `_times`/`clock()` either.

content.text:
Investigation complete. Report below — everything marked "verified" was proven by running probes on your machine today, not just by reading docs.

## Verdict

llama.cpp + Bonsai-27B Q1_0 (3.8 GB) cannot run in andesim hybrid mode today. There are 2 hard blockers, 4 runtime gaps, and 1 usage reality. None are dead ends: a staged path exists, and the first useful cycle numbers (real Q1_0 kernels, real 27B shapes) are reachable **without changing andesim at all**.

## Hard blockers

**1. Guest RAM is capped at 2 GiB, the model needs ~4.5 GB.**
The driver rejects `--mem-size` > 2G (`driver/cmd_run.cpp:395`, `kAe350DramWindowBytes` in `driver/shm.cpp:91`), and QEMU's `andes_ae350` machine itself refuses more ("Cannot model more than 2GB RAM"). There is no mmap on bare metal, so llama.cpp auto-falls-back to no-mmap and reads all 3.8 GB of weights into the heap, plus KV cache + compute buffers = ~4.5 GB total. Lifting this needs coordinated work in three repos: the QEMU machine model (`qemu_andesim`), the vsim RTL platform memory map, and the driver constant.

**2. The bare-metal toolchain has no threads, and llama.cpp core does not compile without them.**
Verified: `/home/nick/nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d` libstdc++ is built without gthreads, so `std::mutex`, `std::thread`, `std::async` do not exist, and newlib's pthread.h has no functions. Four core files fail to compile: `ggml-threading.cpp` (global `std::mutex`), `llama-quant.cpp` (`std::thread`), `llama-model-loader.cpp` (`std::async`), `ggml-cpu.c` (pthread calls). The good news from the code scan: at `n_threads=1` the runtime only ever calls mutex/cond init/lock/unlock/broadcast, never `pthread_create` or `cond_wait` — so simple no-op stubs plus a small llama.cpp patch are enough. This is the main porting work item.

## Runtime gaps in andesim (all small fixes)

- **`_sbrk` has no bounds check** (`runtime/vplat_syscalls.c:364`) and the default stack top is 7 MB (`andesim.ld:95`). Verified live: an 8 MB malloc silently corrupted the stack and crashed with a garbage pointer. Relinking works (I validated a 256 MB heap with `-Wl,--defsym,_stack=0x1FF00000` at `--mem-size 512M`), but andesim should add a heap/stack guard so overflow fails loudly.
- **No `clock_gettime`** — only `_gettimeofday` exists (works, verified). `ggml_time_us()` calls `clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC)`, so it fails to link. Needs a one-function shim in vplat.
- **No argv**: crt0 calls `main(0, NULL, NULL)` (`crt0.S:131`), so `llama-cli` is unusable as-is. The fix is a ~100-line custom driver against `llama.h` only (the `examples/simple/simple.cpp` pattern: load, tokenize, decode loop, greedy sample — needs no `common/` lib).
- **stdin returns EOF** — no interactive chat, fixed-prompt runs only.

## Build-flag matrix (must match the ax45mpv_premium engine: VLEN=512, ELEN=32, no Zfh/Zvfh)

- `GGML_RV_ZFH=OFF`, `GGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF` — neither the RTL nor the hybrid QEMU leg (`-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512`, no zfh flags) supports them. Your user-mode script already hit this.
- `GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF` — repack uses `vsseg4e64` (64-bit vector elements), illegal at ELEN=32.
- Add `-mext-zvlsseg` — the Andes ELF gcc gates segment intrinsics behind it (same as the Linux toolchain in your earlier build), and ggml's quants.c uses `vlseg2e32`.
- `LLAMA_BUILD_COMMON=OFF`, `GGML_OPENMP=OFF`, `CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Generic`, plus `CMAKE_THREAD_LIBS_INIT=""` to satisfy the hard `find_package(Threads REQUIRED)`.
- Good news: `Q1_0` (type 41) is upstream in your tree with an optimized RISC-V RVV dot kernel, VLEN-dispatched at runtime via `vlenb` (bare-metal safe, no hwprobe on the default build path).
- Gotcha found by probe: standalone `--mode fast` pins `-cpu andes-ax46mpv`, which has Zce instead of Zcd, so any FP printf crashes (`c.fld` illegal — even newlib's own libc contains Zcd). Use `-- -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` for fast runs. Hybrid mode is unaffected (CPU is engine-synced).

## What already works (verified by probes)

- C++ end to end on vplat: exceptions, global ctors/dtors, libstdc++ heap — my test ELF linked with `g++ -specs=andesim.specs` and passed.
- HTIF file I/O at 26 MB/s (64 MB in 2.4 s), so the 3.8 GB GGUF loads in ~2.5 min on the QEMU leg.
- Big images survive the handoff: a 3.6 MB-image fixture ran hybrid correctly, including bytes spanning the DLM overlay window at 0x200000 (verified in-ROI on the RTL leg), and printf inside the ROI works on vsim.
- Remember: nothing executes after the ROI end marker (no handback leg), so results must be printed inside the ROI or checked with `--verify`.

## The speed reality for a 27B model

vsim runs at 5-50 kHz (measured 8.9 kHz in the docs' quickstart). One full token of Bonsai-27B is roughly 1-3 G instructions, which is days per token on the RTL. So even after the 2 GiB lift, the hybrid ROI for a 27B model must be one kernel or one layer slice (a single Q1_0 matvec is ~seconds-to-minutes of vsim time), not a full decode. Full-token ROIs are only realistic for ~15M-parameter models.

## Recommended staging

1. **Stage 0 — port kit (llama.cpp side, no andesim changes):** pthread/gthread stubs + `clock_gettime` shim + custom main + Generic toolchain file with the flag matrix above. Prove end-to-end on the fast leg with a small model, then a hybrid kernel ROI.
2. **Stage 1 — Bonsai-27B kernels today, inside 2 GiB:** extract one layer's tensors from the GGUF on the host, run a micro-driver that executes single Q1_0 matvec/attention kernels with ROI markers. Real shapes, real cycle numbers, no platform work.
3. **Stage 2 — andesim feature: >2 GiB DRAM** (QEMU machine + vsim RTL map + driver) for full-model residency. Nice-to-haves along the way: sbrk guard, vplat argv, driver-side model preload into the shared mmap (skips the 2.5-min HTIF load).

All findings are saved to memory (`andesim-llamacpp-hybrid-gaps`) so future sessions start from here.

aiTitle: Investigate Andesim missing features for Llamacpp hybrid mode

content.text:
明白了 — 你的流程就是 hybrid mode 的設計初衷:QEMU 快轉過 load + prompt,vsim 只量一個 kernel iteration。而且你的檢查結果很好:glibc toolchain 有 `libc.a`(static link 可行,test binary 載入位址 0x50000,落在 DRAM window 內),但你目前的 build 是 **dynamically linked**(需要 `ld-linux-riscv64` + kernel)。

Here is the re-study, in simple English.

## Answer

With the glibc build, andesim needs **one new component: a small "proxy kernel" runtime** (like riscv-pk) that gives the static glibc binary the ~25 Linux syscalls it needs, on top of the existing HTIF window. Everything else — the marker/PC triggers, the state transport, the resume driver, the engines — **works unchanged**, because the guest still runs flat M-mode with no paging. Your "measure one iteration" goal fits the existing ROI contract exactly. The only other real platform feature is the >2 GB DRAM lift, needed later for the full 3.8 GB model.

## Why the glibc binary cannot run today

A glibc program does not talk to hardware. At startup `_start` reads `argc/argv/envp/auxv` from the stack (nobody builds that stack on bare metal), and every libc call becomes `ecall` — it expects a Linux kernel to answer. andesim's vplat runtime answers *newlib* function calls, not Linux *syscalls*. That is the whole gap. A kernel is one option; a 200-line syscall emulator is the cheaper one.

## Recommended architecture: "vplat-linux" proxy kernel

A small M-mode payload (`proxy.elf`, built once inside andesim) that:

1. **Loads the app**: reads your static `llama-bench` ELF from the host over the existing HTIF window (26 MB/s measured, ~0.5 s for a 10 MB binary), places its segments in DRAM (they link at 0x50000, inside the window).
2. **Builds the Linux initial stack**: argc/argv/envp/auxv (AT_PAGESZ, AT_PHDR, AT_RANDOM...). This is how you finally get **real command-line args** (`llama-bench -m model.gguf -t 1 ...`) — the driver forwards them into an args file the proxy reads.
3. **Handles `ecall`**: implements ~25-30 syscalls. Most just bridge to the HTIF window ops that already exist and are tested (openat/read/write/lseek/fstat/gettimeofday); the rest are memory management (`brk`, anonymous `mmap` as a bump allocator, `mprotect` no-op) and identity stubs (`set_tid_address`, `rseq`→ENOSYS, `uname`, `getrandom`, `sysinfo` reporting `--mem-size`). `clone` returns ENOSYS → run with `-t 1` (verified earlier: at n_threads=1 ggml never calls `pthread_create`, and uncontended glibc mutexes never reach `futex`).
4. **Does the crt0 duties**: enables caches, `mstatus.FS/VS`, unaligned access — so the existing `mcache_ctl`/write-mask transport keeps working exactly as designed.
5. **Stays in M-mode, paging off, single hart** — the current hybrid envelope. `ecall` from M-mode traps into the proxy's own handler; C++ exceptions stay table-driven (no traps). Syscalls inside the ROI still work (they are MMIO, not device-state), you just avoid them in the measured window.

Then your flow is literally today's flow: markers (or `--trigger pc` + `andesim profile` to find the hot loop) around **one** `ggml_vec_dot_q1_0` / one `mul_mat` call — a counter in the source picks which iteration (`if (++n == K) ROI_begin()`). One iteration of a 27B matvec is ~10-100 M cycles → **minutes to ~1 h on vsim at 9-50 kHz**. Print the checksum inside the ROI (verified working on the RTL leg).

## Why not the other two architectures

- **Boot real Linux in system QEMU, S/U handoff**: this is FRS FR-109 (future). Needs the S-mode CSR envelope finished, paging-on + interrupts inside the ROI, an S/U-capable ax45mpv RTL build (the current `ax45mpv_premium` is compiled M-only), Linux boot plumbing, and still the 2 GB lift. Months of work across three repos.
- **User-mode QEMU fast leg + process handoff**: attractive (your current workflow, no HTIF load), but it needs a new plugin mode, a touched-page capture/copy step, and pointer addresses must all sit below 2 GB — impossible with a 3.8 GB weights buffer anyway until the DRAM lift. More new machinery, same wall.

## The memory math (unchanged blocker for the full model)

The one-iteration ROI working set (~64-200 MB) fits easily. But the **QEMU leg** must still hold the whole process (~4.5 GB) and the AE350 window is 2 GB (QEMU machine + RTL decode + driver cap). So:

- **Bridge (works today)**: slice Bonsai-27B to ~10-15 layers with a gguf-py script (~0.7-1 GB). Per-layer kernel shapes are identical to the full model, so the measured kernel is the real one.
- **Platform feature (stage 2)**: extend the DRAM window to >=6 GB in `qemu_andesim`'s ae350 model + the vsim RTL platform decode + `max_program_mem_bytes()`. That is the single change that makes the untouched 3.8 GB model resident.

## Build-flag carry-over (important)

Your current `build-rv64` uses ggml defaults with `zvfh` — it needed `zvfh=true` even on user-mode QEMU. The hybrid QEMU leg is pinned to `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` (no zvfh) and the RTL has none, so that binary will SIGILL. The static rebuild needs: `-static`, `BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF`, `GGML_RV_ZFH=OFF`, `GGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF`, `GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF` (ELEN=32 forbids the `e64` repack path), keep `-mext-zvlsseg`.

## Work items in andesim

| # | Item | Size |
|---|------|------|
| 1 | `runtime/linux/` proxy kernel: ELF loader + initial stack + ~25 syscalls over the HTIF window + brk/mmap manager | the main task, ~1-2 weeks with tests |
| 2 | Driver: `--runtime linux` mode (launch proxy.elf, pass app ELF + args file, resolve `--pc-start/end` symbols from the app ELF) | small |
| 3 | sbrk-style guard in the proxy's mmap/brk (fail loudly at `--mem-size`, unlike vplat's silent `_sbrk`) | tiny |
| 4 | DRAM window >= 6 GB (QEMU machine + RTL decode + driver constant) | stage 2, cross-repo |

若你同意這個方向,下一步我可以在 andesim repo 寫一份 `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`(照你的 feature-per-session 格式,proxy kernel 拆成獨立小 features),或先寫 `/spec-human` 的 spec 讓你 review 架構。
